title: Matching Q1 Distinguisher for Four-Round KAF
summary: A tight matching quantum attack is known for three rounds, but finding a corresponding Q1 distinguisher for four-round Key-Alternating Feistel remains open.

formal_statement.body: Construct a matching Q1 distinguisher for the 4-round KAF, possibly via collision or period finding.

scope.domain: Post-quantum structural cryptanalysis of four-round Key-Alternating Feistel ciphers.
parameters: Round count: fixed at four for the target KAF construction
Attack setting: Q1, specifying the distinguisher model
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct a matching Q1 distinguisher for the four-round KAF, potentially through collision or period finding.

citations.label: Post-quantum Security of Key-Alternating Feistel Ciphers

progress.summary: The source contrasts the matching attack known for three rounds with the absence of one for four rounds. It identifies collision or period finding as a possible route and notes the difficulty of separating the construction and round function into an asymmetric problem.
citation_labels: Jyotirmoy Basak et al., Post-quantum Security of Key-Alternating Feistel Ciphers
